intro: Khao Kho is packed with resorts competing over photo spots and sea-of-mist views, but Sirinati Khao Kho National Park chooses to sell something that's getting harder to find up here: quiet and privacy · It's a 4-star resort that openly bills itself as Adults Only, set in Khao Kho Subdistrict near several viewpoints and camping spots · There are several room types — Studio, Serenity and Studio Plus — with mountain and garden views and the roomy bathrooms many reviews praise · Rooms start at about ฿1,174/night, with an average score of around 8.0 from real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor.

body.html: The overview, and who Sirinati Khao Kho suits — the shortest possible summary is that Sirinati Khao Kho National Park is a resort for people who come up to Khao Kho to "actually rest" — not to party or bring a big family crew to play together · What sets it apart from the usual Khao Kho resorts is that it states clearly it's Adults Only, which is rare up here since most places focus on families and tour groups · The result is an atmosphere that's quieter and calmer than the area average, well suited to couples who want time to themselves, honeymooners, or anyone working who wants to escape the noise for a couple of quiet nights · Real reviews line up on this: the people most impressed here are the ones who value quiet, cleanliness and a roomy, comfortable bathroom over those chasing lots of activities, a pool, or big-resort facilities · It's a 4-star resort on paper, but in practice it feels more like a mid-sized boutique stay focused mainly on calm · It's still operating normally with reviews coming in steadily, and the average across platforms sits around 8.0, which counts as a good score.

Location and getting there — Sirinati Khao Kho sits at 155 Moo 12, Khao Kho Subdistrict, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun, right in the heart of the Khao Kho tourist zone · The location's strength is being close to a cluster of camping spots and mountain-view cafés within a short walk or drive — some camps and cafés nearby are just a few hundred metres away · From the resort it's a short drive to the Khao Kho viewpoint, and popular landmarks like Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaeo, the wind-turbine field and Phra Borommathat Chedi Kanchanaphisek are roughly a 20–40 min drive depending on the spot · If you're flying in, the nearest airport is Phitsanulok (PHS), which is a fair distance away and means another one-to-two-hour drive up the mountain · One important thing to know about Khao Kho in general is that some stretches of the mountain road are winding and steep — it's best to come in your own car or rent one in good condition with a driver used to mountain roads · If you come in the cold season, which is high season, tourist traffic gets heavy and the road can back up in places, so allow extra travel time and plan each day's sights in nearby clusters so you don't have to drive up and down the mountain repeatedly.

"We stayed as a couple — really quiet, slept like a log. The room was clean, the bathroom bigger than expected, easy mountain views. Waking up early to sip coffee on a quiet balcony is exactly what we came for."

Room types and decor — Sirinati Khao Kho has several room types to choose from by budget and needs · Starting with the Studio Room, the cheapest entry-level room from about ฿1,174/night, good for couples who want a clean, simple room on a manageable budget · Stepping up is the Serenity Room (lower floor) and Serenity Plus (upper floor) group, which gives more space and a better view, with the upper-floor rooms usually getting more open mountain views · The biggest is the Studio Plus at around 75 sqm, spacious and well suited to couples who want a separate sitting area and full privacy · The decor overall is warm and simple in a mountain-resort way, leaning toward easy-on-the-eyes comfort rather than flash · What real reviews mention most often about the rooms is the roomy, clean bathroom with a walk-in shower, a full set of bathroom amenities, and many reviews praise having plenty of power outlets for charging devices — a small detail today's travellers care about · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV with satellite channels, tea and coffee facilities, and a garden or mountain view depending on the room type · One thing worth knowing is that this is a building that's been open for a while, and some of the decor and facilities are starting to show wear and need upkeep, which comes through in some reviews mentioning the consistency of room condition · If views matter to you in particular, ask for an upper-floor room or one facing the mountains right at the time of booking.

Facilities (and what's missing) — to set expectations right, this has to be said up front: Sirinati Khao Kho has no swimming pool · That's the first thing to know, because if your picture of Khao Kho involves a pool to soak in, this isn't the place for you on that front · What the resort does have, and does well, is its garden, terrace and outdoor seating that look out to the mountains — good for sipping morning coffee or catching the cool evening breeze · There's a garden-view restaurant and a lobby bar for a light drink · There's free Wi-Fi in common areas, free private parking, room service during limited hours, an airport shuttle (at a fee), and even a meeting room of around 200 sqm for small seminar groups · The reception desk is open roughly 7:30 AM–10:00 PM, which means if you arrive very late you should let them know in advance · Overall the facilities here are at the level of "enough for a quiet getaway" rather than a full activity resort — which fits the Adults Only concept that puts calm first.

Food and drink — the restaurant at Sirinati Khao Kho serves both Thai and international dishes, with vegetarian options too, and has seating that looks out over the garden and mountains, making meals feel relaxed · Breakfast is buffet-style, and on some packages the room rate may not include breakfast, with an extra charge of about ฿500 per adult — this is a point to check carefully when booking, whether your chosen rate includes breakfast or not, so the budget doesn't creep up without you meaning it to · Real reviews on the food are fairly mixed: some praise the nice atmosphere and tasty hot dishes, but a few mention breakfast service that isn't quite consistent yet at times, such as slow refills or limited options on days when the place isn't full · The upside of the location is that the area around Khao Kho has plenty of cafés and mountain-view restaurants to drive out and try, so many people choose to have breakfast or coffee at the resort and then head out to find a good spot for other meals — which fits the Khao Kho travel style nicely.

Service — service is a point that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews, especially the staff's friendliness and attentive care · Many couple reviews rate the overall experience highly and mention the sense of privacy that comes from the resort being adults-only · There's basic help like recommending places to visit, sorting out transport, and general upkeep · That said, to be straight about it, a few voices note that the consistency of service and upkeep in some spots isn't always even across every period, especially on busy days or when staff are limited · This is a common trait of mid-sized mountain resorts that don't have the large teams of in-city chain hotels · Overall the service still counts as good and friendly, suited to people who understand the nature of mountain stays and aren't expecting five-star in-city hotel service.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling together voices from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent and makes the decision easier · On the praise side: the quiet and privacy from being Adults Only, clean rooms, a roomy and clean bathroom with a walk-in shower, plenty of power outlets in the room, easy mountain and garden views, comfy beds that many reviews score highly, and friendly staff · There's a couple review that scored their two-person trip as high as around 8.7, which reflects that couples are the guests this place matches best · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most is some facilities starting to age and needing upkeep as the building gets older, cleanliness and service consistency that isn't always even at times, gaps in breakfast service on some days, and a feeling that some facilities aren't quite worth it against high-season rates · And crucially, there's no swimming pool, a limitation you have to accept before booking · Most of these gripes are things you can manage by setting expectations right and picking the right period/rate, rather than big problems that would put people off coming back.

"Loved that it's adults only — not crowded, quiet for the price · The one gripe is that some corners of the room and the resort are getting old and could use a bit more upkeep, but if you come to rest quietly it's worth it."

Price and value — the starting price for the Studio Room is about ฿1,174/night at normal rates, which is manageable for a resort tagged 4-star on Khao Kho · The Serenity and Studio Plus rooms move up with size and view, and in high season or on long weekends every room type can climb a fair bit, with reviews noting bookings at rates of around the low two-thousands per night at times · Compared with the famous sea-of-mist resorts on Khao Kho that start at a similar level, Sirinati's selling point isn't a "sea of mist off the balcony" that so many people chase, but rather quiet, Adults Only privacy, a roomy bathroom and a clean room · So the value here depends on what you value — if you're a couple wanting a quiet night away from the sound of kids and tour groups, the money buys back genuine calm · But if you expect a pool, full facilities and the sea-of-mist views you see in social posts, you might feel there are other options on Khao Kho that are better value for the same budget · The advice is to compare prices across several platforms and check clearly whether the rate includes breakfast before you book.

What to know before booking — there are several things that make the stay go smoother · One, this is Adults Only, so if you're planning to bring children this isn't the option — look for a Khao Kho resort that takes families instead · Two, there's no swimming pool; if a pool is a must for your trip, skip ahead to somewhere else · Three, check clearly whether your booked rate includes breakfast, since the breakfast buffet carries an extra charge of about ฿500/adult · Four, if views matter, ask for an upper-floor room or one facing the mountains right at booking · Five, the reception desk is open roughly 7:30 AM–10:00 PM, so let them know in advance if you arrive late · Six, some stretches of the Khao Kho road are winding and steep — come in a car in good condition and allow extra time, especially in the cold season when traffic is heavy · Seven, in the late-rains-to-early-cold high season (November–January) rooms fill up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and pick a free-cancellation option to be safe if your plans aren't firm yet.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Sirinati Khao Kho National Park is the resort that suits couples and adults who come up to Khao Kho for a quiet, private getaway at a manageable starting price · The clear strengths are the quiet from being Adults Only, clean rooms, a roomy bathroom, comfy beds and a relaxing mountain-garden setting · But you have to accept that this place has no swimming pool, doesn't sell sea-of-mist views off the balcony like the famous resorts, and some facilities are starting to age with the building, with service and cleanliness consistency that isn't always even · If you're after a sea of mist for photos, a pool, or bringing kids, this may not be the answer, and you should look at other options on Khao Kho instead · But for a quiet night for two, away from the bustle, with a roomy bathroom and a comfy bed on a budget that isn't expensive — Sirinati Khao Kho meets that need well, and that's why many couples rate their own trip so highly.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Sirinati Khao Kho National Park

faq.q: Where is Sirinati Khao Kho National Park, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The resort sits at 155 Moo 12, Khao Kho Subdistrict, Khao Kho District, Phetchabun 67270, in the heart of the Khao Kho tourist zone · It's near a cluster of camps and cafés within a few hundred metres, and a short drive from the Khao Kho viewpoint, Wat Phra That Pha Son Kaeo and the wind-turbine field · Some stretches of the mountain road are winding and steep, so we'd recommend coming in your own car in good condition.

faq.q: Does Sirinati Khao Kho take children, and is it really Adults Only?
faq.a: Yes — this is an adults-only resort · The main selling point is quiet and privacy, well suited to couples and adults who want a calm getaway · If you're planning to bring children, look for a Khao Kho resort that takes families instead.

faq.q: Does Sirinati Khao Kho have a pool, and is breakfast included in the price?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool — this place leans on quiet, the garden and mountain-view seating rather than activities · Breakfast is buffet-style, and some rates carry an extra charge of about ฿500 per adult, so check clearly when booking whether your chosen rate includes breakfast or not.

faq.q: What's the starting price at Sirinati Khao Kho, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,174/night for a Studio Room · There's the Serenity Room (lower floor) and Serenity Plus (upper floor, with a more open mountain view) group, and the biggest room, Studio Plus, at around 75 sqm · In high season prices can climb to around the low two-thousands per night, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who does Sirinati Khao Kho suit best?
faq.a: It suits couples and adults who come up to Khao Kho for a quiet, private getaway very well, valuing calm, a roomy bathroom, clean rooms and a comfy bed over lots of activities or a pool · There's a couple review that scored their two-person trip as high as around 8.7, which reflects that couples are the group this place matches best.

faq.q: What are the things to watch out for at Sirinati Khao Kho?
faq.a: Real reviews mention some facilities starting to age and needing upkeep, cleanliness and service that isn't always even across every period, and gaps in breakfast service on some days · Plus the fact that there's no swimming pool · If you set expectations mainly around quiet and value, and pick the right room/period, the stay goes a lot more smoothly.
